newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden FinMin says to close down Securum.
newsitem.headline: Sweden FinMin says to close down Securum.

text.p: Sweden's Finance Minister Erik Asbrink said on Tuesday that the state was to close down Securum in 1997, a state company that took over bank's collateral for bad loans, mainly property, in the early 1990s.
Presenting the supplementary budget, Asbrink said the assets of Securum would be transferred to Vasakronan.
Vasakronan is a state owned property company.
Securum was formed to take over assets pledged by Nordbanken during the Swedish bank crisis in the early 1990s and aimed to divest all holdings at reasonable prices.
"In the end slightly more than half of the 24 billion crowns which was added (by the government) to cover the calculated losses will be regained," the government said.
The government also wants to sell its stake in Swedish central securities depositories Vardepapperscentalen (VPC) and make investments in Sweden's financial infrastructure.
The country's derivates trading operator OM and the stock exchange are currently negotiating a possible merger.
The government said it wants to keep a hold in one of the core businesses of the financial sector.
It suggested, therefore, that 500 million crowns from a possible sale of the shares in VPC may be used to buy such a stake.
Finance Minister Asbrink appointed Stefan Ingves, deputy governor of Sweden's central bank, the Riksbank, to represent the government in future negotiations.
